keyFindings.description: Normalize truncates and fills a missing row but never floors an empty detail on a failing row; the wire allows it (legion-api.ts:297 rows[].detail z.string()) and the state view refuses it (legion-api.ts:119 open[].detail nonEmptyString), so one session reporting {name, ok:false, detail:""} makes GET /legion/v1/state fail the strict parse in every plugin reader (daemon-client.ts:211-213 -> read_state, read_record and handoff_complete's record read, tools.ts:202/216/234). Reproduced from the contracts state fixture with one open detail blanked: issues.LEGION-208.workers.implementer.claim.capabilities.open.0.detail: Too small. Persisted and reloaded at boot, so it survives a restart. Reachable from capability-report.ts:440-442 failed(firstLine(messageFor(error))) on an error with an empty message, and from any plugin build since the daemon never refuses. Fix: floor the empty detail in Normalize beside the existing filler, and give the claim-only locator's incarnation a sentinel (or relax legionCapabilityReportView to z.string()).

The hook runs the store write on r.Context() while the handler built the disconnect-proof ctx at :142 (context.WithoutCancel, server.go:268) and used it for m.Handle. A client disconnect (the plugin's ready retry on a timeout, a pod dying) cancels PutCapabilityReport, the daemon logs the misleading ERROR could-not-be-persisted (daemon.go:862-864) and a restart renders that session unreported. One-token fix: pass ctx.

The abort listener is attached after discoverMCPServers resolves; if the 8 s budget aborted during loadMCPConfigs/discoverMCPServers it never fires, and the finally never runs when waitForPendingConnections never settles (the case the comment at :243-245 claims is handled), so the second MCP client set leaks for the session. Fix: if (signal.aborted) void tearDown(); after :251.
